title: MM-Path: Multi-modal, Multi-granularity Path Representation Learning

problem.claim: Effective path representations are needed in intelligent transportation.

gap.claim: Existing pre-trained path representation models focus mainly on topological structures from road networks and overlook geometric and contextual features from path-related images; multimodal granularity differences and data heterogeneity further hinder semantic alignment and fusion.

contributions.claim: MM-Path is a framework for learning generic path representations by integrating road-path and image-path modalities.
A multi-granularity alignment strategy associates nodes, road sub-paths, and road paths with corresponding image patches.
A graph-based cross-modal residual fusion component fuses information across modalities and granularities.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe MM-Path as a novel multi-modal, multi-granularity path representation learning framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on two large-scale real-world datasets.
The authors report evaluation under two downstream tasks.
The authors report that these experiments validate the effectiveness of MM-Path.

narrative_sequence.summary: Path representations are increasingly important in intelligent transportation.
Existing approaches underuse image-based geometric and contextual information, and multimodal alignment is difficult across granularities and heterogeneous data.
Combining modalities may improve representation accuracy and generalization.
MM-Path integrates road paths and image paths using multi-granularity alignment and graph-based cross-modal residual fusion.
The framework is evaluated on two real-world datasets across two downstream tasks.

source_observation.claim: Aligning corresponding entities across multiple granularities can synchronize local details and global context.

interpretation.claim: Multimodal representation systems may benefit from explicit alignment at several structural scales.

application.claim: When combining structured paths with imagery, design alignment links between fine-grained elements and whole-path representations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which downstream settings or data conditions limit this approach.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the model architecture beyond the named alignment and fusion components.
The abstract does not provide dataset names, task definitions, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not report ablations, computational costs, or failure cases.
